lines.text:
A Visit to the Museum

Last weekend, my family visited the National History Museum in the city centre. Entry was free, but we made a small donation at the reception desk.

The ground floor had a permanent exhibition about ancient Egypt. We saw mummies in glass cases, stone tablets covered in hieroglyphics, and golden jewellery that was over three thousand years old. Each object had a small label with a description, the date, and where it was found.

On the first floor, there was a temporary exhibition about the Roman Empire. It included weapons, coins, and a model of a Roman villa. An audio guide was available, and I borrowed one so I could listen to explanations as I walked around. The narrator described how Roman soldiers lived and what they ate.

The top floor was dedicated to natural history. There were dinosaur skeletons, fossils, and stuffed animals displayed in recreations of their natural habitats. A huge model of a blue whale hung from the ceiling, and my younger brother could not stop staring at it.

In the interactive gallery, children could touch replica artefacts and dress up in historical costumes. There were also touchscreen displays with quizzes about what we had seen.

We spent three hours in the museum and still did not see everything. My father said we should come back to visit the art gallery next door. Museums are a wonderful way to learn about history without reading a textbook.
